Mozilla just introduced Firefox Enterprise, and I think the timing is interesting. Most companies rely on Chrome or Edge, which are both built on Chromium. Firefox gives them an independent browser engine, and now there's an enterprise offering with a management console they can run on their own infrastructure. IT teams can manage browser policies, access, data movement, and AI usage without handing over control of the management layer. Mozilla is starting in Europe, where digital sovereignty has become a pretty big topic. Nice to see another serious option for enterprise browsers.

## Firefox Enterprise

Launching today

Firefox for enterprises that want control of their data

Firefox Enterprise brings Mozilla's independent browser technology to organizations that want more control over their IT infrastructure and data. Built on the Gecko engine, it offers a self-hosted management console for centrally managing browser policies, access, data movement, and AI usage. It works alongside existing identity, security, and device management systems, helping enterprises reduce dependence on dominant browser ecosystems.

This is the browser I've been searching for, it takes the current browser UI/UX paradigms and turns them on their head to use a more contextual computing model and an emphasis on tasks over sites. Add in the command palette and extensive keyboard shortcuts and it's really increasing my productivity in just a short time using it. It's certainly still early and rough around the edges, I'm very much looking forward to custom search engines, extensions, more minimalist and custom to workspace icons and it will be the only browser I have open. I'm seriously excited about its future! I also love how responsive the team is, that's a huge benefit!

#### What's great [...] SigmaOS markets itself as "the first browser specifically made for work" and targets "students managing courses" and "founders building startups." Yet it fundamentally fails at the most basic institutional workflow: SSO redirect authentication. Without this fundamental and game-breaking failure, it would easily be a 5 star browser and I would have no complaints. Every university library system (Ex Libris, OCLC), corporate SSO (Okta, SAML), government portal, and B2B platform uses redirect-based authentication. You save the redirect URL, click it, authenticate, and access your tools. This is Web 101 for institutional users.
